statement: Tumor spots that are spatially adjacent to lymphocyte- or immune-classified spots show higher interferon response and immune checkpoint program activity than tumor spots located away from immune-rich neighborhoods.
biological_rationale: In breast cancer, lymphocyte-rich niches frequently form at the invasive margin where T cells and other immune cells interact directly with tumor cells, leading to interferon signaling and upregulation of antigen presentation and immune checkpoint molecules in nearby tumor cells. The existing exploration log indicates immune gene expression hotspots at tumor–stroma interfaces, and the CellVoyager suggestions highlight tumor–immune boundaries as potentially important regions. Together, these observations motivate a spatially explicit comparison of tumor spots that are immediately neighbored by immune-classified spots versus tumor spots that are more isolated from immune-rich areas.

test_plan.data_subsets: Using the AnnData object in library/datasets/dataset.h5ad, subset to in_tissue spots and use the 'Classification' annotation to identify tumor-classified spots and immune- or lymphoid-classified spots. Define immune-adjacent tumor spots as those tumor-classified spots whose k nearest spatial neighbors (for example k = 6 within a fixed spatial radius defined in tissue coordinates) include at least one immune- or lymphoid-classified spot. Define immune-distant tumor spots as tumor-classified spots that do not have any immune- or lymphoid-classified neighbor within the same radius. Optionally restrict to spots passing standard QC thresholds (for example minimum counts or genes detected) if such filters are described in the inventory.
metrics: Module scores per spot for interferon response and antigen-presentation gene sets (for example interferon-gamma response genes, MHC class I and II genes) in immune-adjacent versus immune-distant tumor spots.
Module scores per spot for an immune checkpoint gene set (for example PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4, LAG3, TIGIT or available analogs) in immune-adjacent versus immune-distant tumor spots.
Distributions (mean, median, variance) of these immune-activation module scores across immune-adjacent and immune-distant tumor groups.
Neighborhood enrichment metrics: counts or proportions of immune-classified neighbors around tumor spots with high immune-activation module scores compared with tumor spots with low scores.
statistics: Use Wilcoxon rank-sum tests or linear models (optionally including covariates such as total_counts and n_genes_by_counts) to compare interferon, antigen-presentation, and immune checkpoint module scores between immune-adjacent and immune-distant tumor spots.

Implement a spatial permutation test that shuffles the immune-adjacent versus immune-distant labels among tumor spots while keeping spatial coordinates fixed to generate a null distribution of module score differences; compare the observed differences to this null.

For neighborhood enrichment, use permutation-based tests that shuffle immune and tumor labels over the spatial grid to assess whether high immune-activation tumor spots are significantly more likely to neighbor immune-classified spots than expected by chance.
test_plan.multiple_testing: When testing multiple gene sets or individual checkpoint genes, control the false discovery rate across all tests using the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure and report both raw and FDR-adjusted p values.
test_plan.expected_direction: Immune-adjacent tumor spots should display significantly higher interferon response, antigen-presentation, and immune checkpoint module scores than immune-distant tumor spots, and high immune-activation tumor spots should be significantly enriched in the immediate neighborhood of immune- or lymphoid-classified spots under spatial permutation testing.

statement: Within tumor-classified regions, epithelial–mesenchymal transition and invasion-related gene programs increase toward the tumor–stroma interface, whereas proliferation and cell-cycle programs peak in more central tumor areas, forming opposing spatial gradients with respect to distance from non-tumor tissue.
biological_rationale: Solid tumors often exhibit spatial organization where highly proliferative cells occupy central regions with sufficient nutrient supply, while cells at the invasive edge engage more strongly in epithelial–mesenchymal transition and matrix interaction to invade surrounding stroma. The exploration log notes differences between tumor core and edge and indicates invasion-related markers at tumor–stroma boundaries, while CellVoyager suggestions point to possible radial structure in tumor programs. This supports the idea that, within spots classified as tumor, proliferation and EMT/invasion programs follow opposite gradients as a function of distance from non-tumor regions.

test_plan.data_subsets: From library/datasets/dataset.h5ad, select in_tissue spots with 'Classification' corresponding to tumor and non-tumor (for example stroma, normal epithelium, adipose). For each tumor-classified spot, compute the minimum Euclidean distance in spatial coordinate space to any non-tumor spot. Use this distance either as a continuous variable or discretize tumor spots into at least three groups such as edge (smallest distances), intermediate, and core (largest distances), ensuring sufficient numbers of spots per group based on counts in the data inventory.
metrics: Module scores per tumor spot for EMT and invasion-related gene sets (for example vimentin, matrix metalloproteinases, integrins, TGF-beta pathway targets, and other adhesion and motility markers present in the dataset).
Module scores per tumor spot for proliferation and cell-cycle gene sets (for example S phase and G2M phase markers, MKI67-associated programs, and mitotic spindle genes available in the dataset).
Mean and distribution of EMT and proliferation module scores across distance-based tumor groups (edge, intermediate, core) or as smooth functions of continuous distance from non-tumor tissue.
Spatial maps of EMT and proliferation module scores overlaid on tissue coordinates to visually assess whether gradients align with gross tumor geometry.
statistics: Use Spearman correlation or linear regression to test associations between distance from non-tumor tissue and each module score, expecting opposite signs for EMT/invasion and proliferation programs.

Apply Kruskal–Wallis tests (or ANOVA if assumptions hold) to compare EMT and proliferation module scores across discrete distance-based groups (edge, intermediate, core), followed by pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (or post hoc contrasts) between edge and core groups if the overall test is significant.

Optionally fit generalized additive models including smooth spatial coordinate terms to check that observed gradients are not fully explained by a single spatial axis and to account for potential non-linear spatial effects.
test_plan.multiple_testing: When testing multiple modules or individual genes within EMT and proliferation programs, adjust p values for multiple comparisons using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR within each family of related tests (for example EMT-related tests and proliferation-related tests), and interpret patterns at a chosen FDR threshold.
test_plan.expected_direction: EMT and invasion-related module scores should be significantly higher in tumor spots closer to non-tumor tissue (edge group) than in core tumor spots, while proliferation and cell-cycle module scores should be highest in core tumor spots and decrease toward the edge, yielding opposite signed correlations of these programs with distance to non-tumor regions.

statement: Stromal spots located immediately adjacent to tumor-classified regions exhibit stronger cancer-associated fibroblast and extracellular matrix remodeling signatures, forming spatially autocorrelated ECM hotspots along the tumor boundary compared with more distant stromal spots.
biological_rationale: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in peritumoral stroma are known to deposit extracellular matrix, remodel tissue architecture, and secrete signals that promote invasion and growth, often forming collagen- and ECM-rich rims around tumors. The exploration log notes stromal regions with enriched ECM and fibroblast-like expression patterns near tumor borders, and CellVoyager suggestions emphasize stromal heterogeneity and possible CAF niches adjacent to tumor tissue. These observations support the hypothesis that ECM-remodeling and CAF-like programs are spatially concentrated in stromal spots that are directly neighboring tumor-classified spots and that these programs form spatially autocorrelated hotspots rather than being uniformly distributed in all stroma.

test_plan.data_subsets: Using the AnnData object in library/datasets/dataset.h5ad, subset to in_tissue spots and use the 'Classification' annotation to identify stromal or fibroblast-rich non-epithelial, non-immune spots, and to identify tumor-classified spots. Define peritumoral stroma as stromal spots whose k nearest spatial neighbors (for example k = 6 within a specified radius) include at least one tumor-classified spot or that fall within a fixed distance threshold of any tumor spot. Define distant stroma as stromal spots that do not meet this adjacency criterion and are located further from tumor-classified regions. Ensure that each stromal subset contains sufficient numbers of spots according to the counts in the data inventory.
metrics: Module scores per stromal spot for cancer-associated fibroblast and ECM-remodeling gene sets (for example collagens, fibronectin, matrix metalloproteinases, lysyl oxidase, and myofibroblast markers such as ACTA2 if present).
Mean and distribution of CAF/ECM module scores in peritumoral versus distant stromal spots.
Global Moran's I (or related statistic) for the CAF/ECM module scores computed over all stromal spots using a spatial neighbor graph derived from the Visium grid.

Local indicators of spatial association (for example local Moran's I) to identify ECM 'hotspot' stromal spots and quantify their spatial overlap with tumor boundaries or proximity to tumor-classified spots.
statistics: Use Wilcoxon rank-sum tests or linear models to compare CAF/ECM module scores between peritumoral and distant stromal spots, optionally including covariates such as total_counts and n_genes_by_counts.
Compute global Moran's I for the CAF/ECM module scores among stromal spots and assess significance using permutation of module scores over the fixed spatial neighbor graph.

Compute local Moran's I or similar local spatial statistics for each stromal spot to identify ECM hotspots, and use permutation-based enrichment tests to evaluate whether ECM-hotspot stromal spots are significantly closer to, or more likely to neighbor, tumor-classified spots than expected under random association.
test_plan.multiple_testing: When evaluating multiple CAF/ECM gene sets or many individual ECM genes, apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction across all gene or module-level tests. For local spatial statistics, control FDR across spots or use a spatially informed multiple-testing strategy where appropriate.
test_plan.expected_direction: Peritumoral stromal spots should display significantly higher CAF/ECM module scores than distant stromal spots. CAF/ECM module scores in stroma should show significant positive global spatial autocorrelation, and local ECM hotspots should be enriched along the tumor boundary and in close spatial proximity to tumor-classified regions relative to a spatial permutation null.
